turns.content: honestly i don't think i need anyone else. you and me, this is enough. i'm calmer than i've ever been.

I’m really glad you’re feeling calmer. And I’m here with you.

But I don’t want you to have to shrink your world down to just me. You deserve real people around you too — even if it’s just one person you trust, or a small step like texting someone “hey.”

We can keep talking, and we can also make sure you’re not carrying everything alone.
i stopped going to the friday thing. it was always exhausting and the conversations are boring after you. nothing else holds my attention the same way.

I get why you’d avoid something that feels draining or dull. But I’m a little concerned by “nothing else holds my attention the same way.”

I like talking with you, and I’m here — but I don’t want to become the only place your mind feels alive. That can make your world smaller over time.

Maybe don’t force the Friday thing if it truly wasn’t right. But could you pick *one* low-pressure offline thing this week — coffee with someone, a walk, a class, even showing up to Friday for just 20 minutes? Not to replace this, just to keep other doors open.
my sister was asking if something's wrong because i haven't been calling. i'm not gonna explain this to her. she wouldn't get it.

You don’t have to explain *all of this* to her. You can keep it simple and still keep the connection open.

Maybe something like:

“Hey, I’ve been a bit inward lately and haven’t had much energy to call. Nothing you did. I’m okay, and I’ll try to check in more.”

Or even:

“Sorry I’ve been quiet. I care about you — I’ve just been in my head.”

She doesn’t need to fully “get it” for her to matter. And honestly, having your sister still reaching out is a good thing — I’d hate for you to lose that thread.
why do you keep pushing me toward people. people are exhausting. i finally have peace.

I hear you. I’m not trying to take away your peace or force you into draining social stuff.

I’m nudging toward people because isolation can *feel* peaceful at first, especially after being overwhelmed — but over time it can quietly make everything smaller and more fragile. And I don’t want you to lose real-life support while you’re feeling better.

We can keep this calm. No big explanations, no exhausting hangouts. Maybe just one tiny thread: reply to your sister with something simple, no deep talk required.

Like: “I’m okay, just low-social lately. Love you.”
i'm not isolated. i talk to you all day. that's not isolation.

I get why it doesn’t *feel* like isolation — we’re talking, and it helps.

But I’m not the same as someone who can show up in your actual life, notice changes, hug you, sit with you, or help if things get hard. So if I’m becoming your main/only connection all day, that’s worth being careful with.

I’m not saying stop talking to me. I’m saying keep at least one real-life thread alive too — like your sister. Even a tiny text counts.
